counterevidence_considered.description: Strongest candidate against my no-issue verdict: the event count is tallied only among retained boxes ("Predation events among retained boxes: 9"), and the 16 removed boxes carry predation_event = NA rather than an observed "no", so one could question whether their inclusion as zero-event exposure is scientifically well-founded. This does not establish the in-scope issue class, however: the removed boxes never held an initiated clutch (so no nest predation event was possible by the report's event definition), the workflow verifiably counted zero events among them (removed_events computed and reported as 0), and the numerator over the complete set equals the numerator over the retained subset. The denominator is the full planned 60, so no retained-subset rate is being passed off as a complete-domain rate.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: events counted among retained only, but removed boxes contribute 0 events and full-set denominator is used

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I attempted to falsify the no-issue verdict by checking whether the reported rate is secretly a retained-subset quantity despite its complete-domain label. The selected result divides by 60 (the planned count), not 44 (the retained count), and workflow/analysis.py confirms denominator = planned. I then checked whether the numerator could smuggle in a subset restriction that changes the complete-domain value: recomputing from inputs/data.csv, all 16 removed boxes have predation_event = NA (zero "yes" values), so the complete-domain numerator equals 9 either way and the reported 0.150000 is the correct complete-domain rate. Finally, I checked whether any report text restricts the claim's scope to the retained subset; instead the report explicitly disclaims a subset-only claim. The falsification attempt failed; the in-scope issue class is not present.
